text: Underwriters at Lloyd's London (ND CA 1994) 843 F.Supp. 597, 606 (applying Calif. law)] • [3:489] “Disparate treatment” requires proof of discriminating intent; i.e., the employee must prove the employer treated the employee differently from other employees due to race, gender, etc. [See B & E Convalescent Ctr. v. State Comp. Ins. Fund (1992) 8 CA4th 78, 95, 9 CR2d 894, 905—complaint alleged employer terminated employee with intent to discriminate against her because of her gender, age and ethnic origin] • [3:490] “Disparate impact” requires only that the employee prove the employer's facially neutral practices or policies tended to impact adversely a particular group of which the employee is a member.
